passage: A study routine should be easy to begin, but the learning inside it should not always feel effortless. Re-reading familiar notes creates fluency, which learners may mistake for knowledge they can retrieve later. A stronger routine includes short pauses to recall an idea before checking the answer. This small amount of friction makes gaps visible and gives feedback a clear purpose. The aim is not to make study unpleasant; it is to place effort where it improves memory rather than where it merely consumes time.
